title: cPanel EmailTrack SQL Injection Flaw Lets Attackers Execute Code as Root
content_md: cPanel has disclosed a critical SQL injection vulnerability in its EmailTrack functionality that could allow a low-privileged, authenticated account to execute code as root. Tracked as CVE-2026-67401, the flaw affects all supported cPanel & WHM releases and requires immediate patching. According to cPanel’s September 8 security advisory, exploitation begins with an authenticated cPanel account that has mail-related privileges. cPanel EmailTrack SQL Injection Flaw The vendor said attackers can abuse this access through EmailTrack to create arbitrary files on the underlying server. The result is code execution as the root user, giving an attacker complete control of the host. The advisory describes the bug as SQL injection, but does not publish technical exploitation details, proof-of-concept code, affected request parameters, or a CVSS score. That restraint matters: defenders should avoid assuming that the absence of public exploit code means exposure is low. On shared hosting infrastructure, a compromised customer-level account with suitable mail permissions could become a route from a tenant context to the server’s most privileged account.
